blindSourceSummaries: An encyclopaedia overview of the country's LGBT rights: the national legal timeline - recognition of same-sex unions and marriage (2011/2013 top-court rulings), adoption, discrimination protections, gender identity and expression (the March 2018 self-declaration rulings allowing name/gender-marker change without surgery), conversion therapy, military service and blood donation, plus a section listing non-binary marker rules by federative unit. Framework is national; unit-level variation is not covered by this page.

An international LGBT-rights organisation's country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations legal throughout the country; legal gender recognition possible by self-determination; a 2019 top-court ruling prohibits discrimination and hate crimes on SOGI grounds; marriage equality since 2013 with active repeal efforts in the national legislature; the country continues to have one of the highest recorded rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; 3,000+ openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections; a 2025 higher-court ruling allows nonbinary civil-registry amendments; executive pro-rights stance versus a conservative legislature generating a surge of anti-LGBTQ proposals.

A law-firm guide to LGBTQ+ legal rights for expats (updated April 2026): protections were established by the country's top court rather than statute - same-sex marriage, spousal-visa equality, joint adoption, name and gender-marker change without surgery, and criminalisation of homophobia/transphobia as equivalent to racism; major cities are broadly welcoming with legal infrastructure accustomed to same-sex marriages and name changes; the guide states smaller cities and rural areas may present more social friction, 'though the legal rights are identical nationwide'.
